tools.name: attach_project
tools.description: Attach a local Maya tool project to the live Maya Python session by adding its root (and optional src/ directory) to sys.path. Use this once before run_entrypoint/run_script. Set DCC_MCP_MAYA_DEV_ROOTS to restrict trusted roots in studio deployments.

name.description: Optional session label; defaults to the directory name.

include_src.description: Also add project_root/src to sys.path when it exists.

make_active.description: Make this project the default target for later dev tools.

tools.name: reload_modules
tools.description: Purge or reload modules that belong to the attached development project. Default mode=purge removes matching modules from sys.modules so the next import sees edited files, which is usually safer than importlib.reload in long-lived Maya sessions.

project_name.description: Attached project label; defaults to the active project.

package_prefixes.description: Override package/module prefixes for this reload.

mode.description: purge removes modules from sys.modules; reload calls importlib.reload.

tools.name: run_entrypoint
tools.description: Run a callable from the attached development project inside Maya, with stdout/stderr/traceback captured into the result envelope. Use target="package.module:function" or module + callable.

module.description: Python module to import when target is not supplied.

project_name.description: Attached project label; defaults to the active project.

tools.name: run_script
tools.description: Run a project-local .py script with sys.argv, cwd, stdout/stderr, traceback, and elapsed time captured. The script must live under the attached project root.

script_path.description: Project-relative or absolute path to a .py file under the attached root.

tools.name: start_debugpy
tools.description: Try to start an optional debugpy listener inside the Maya process so Cursor or VS Code can attach breakpoints before MCP-triggered project code runs. wait_for_client.description: Block until an IDE attaches. Usually keep false for agent workflows.

configure_python.description: Configure debugpy's Python executable from the Maya runtime when possible.

python_executable.description: Optional explicit Python/mayapy executable for debugpy.configure(python=...).

log_dir.description: Optional directory passed to debugpy.log_to; defaults to DCC_MCP_MAYA_DEBUGPY_LOG_DIR.

tools.name: capture_ui
tools.description: Capture the Maya main window or a named Qt widget as a base64 PNG. Use this for debugging custom tool windows and dock controls; use maya-render capture_viewport for viewport imagery.

tools.name: sample_pixel_region
tools.description: Sample a rectangular region of one texture or render target on a grid and report per sample its coordinates and decoded channel values, plus per-channel min, max, and mean over the samples. event_id replays to that event first, so the readback is the target's contents at that point in the frame. Requires an uncompressed numeric format: block-compressed, packed, and special formats come back as a structured unsupported result naming the reason instead of sampled zeros. The grid decides how much of the region is read, so a grid coarser than the region makes the statistics a sampled estimate, which the payload reports in estimate and estimate_method. Use before reasoning about what a region contains, and as the primitive diagnose_pixel_values scans. Not for one pixel's value - use renderdoc_inspect__get_texture_data with include_pixels, or renderdoc_debug__pick_pixel to find which draw touched it.

tools.name: diagnose_pixel_values
tools.description: Scan a region of one texture or render target for NaN, Inf, negative, and out-of-band float values, returning per check how many values matched, up to max_anomalies coordinates per check, per-channel statistics, and an overall anomaly texel count. event_id replays to that event first. NaN and Inf only exist in a floating-point format and a negative value is only a signal in one, so an integer format reports each check as not applicable with the reason rather than as four zeros. Regions larger than max_texels are scanned with a stride, and the payload then reports the stride, the sampled flag, and the estimate method. Use to find where a frame starts producing garbage before debugging a single pixel. Not for why one pixel has the value it has - use renderdoc_debug__pixel_history.

tools.name: get_frame_overview
tools.description: Report what one capture contains in a single replay - API and frame properties, action counts broken into draws, dispatches, and clears, the root-level pass structure with per-pass draw, index, and output-target load, the largest textures and the format histogram, whether this driver exposes counters and whether one of them carries GPU duration, the debug messages a replay to the last event produced, and the structural signals worth acting on, such as a degraded replay, a frame with no draws, a driver with counters but no duration counter, or one texture that dominates texture memory. Pass triangle counts are derived from API draw parameters and the signals are thresholds over structure: both are reported as estimates in estimate_fields and in the summary, and neither is a measurement. Use as the first call on an unfamiliar capture. Not for per-draw cost - use renderdoc_perf__get_action_timing.

tools.name: get_draw_call_state
tools.description: Snapshot everything one draw executed with in one call - the action itself with its depth and parent event id, the full pipeline state for that event, and the bound shader stages with their reflection, signatures, constant blocks, and resource bindings. stages defaults to the stages the pipeline state reports as bound; include_constant_buffers and include_source widen the shader payload at the cost of size. One stage this capture cannot reflect is reported as an errored entry while the other stages are still returned. Use when the question is what this draw was actually running with. Not for stepping through what the shader did to one pixel - use renderdoc_debug__debug_pixel.

tools.name: analyze_render_passes
tools.description: Report the frame's pass structure from the action tree alone, without a counter - one entry per pass with its event range, action, draw, dispatch, and clear counts, index and instance totals, output and depth targets, and an optional list of its actions. pass_depth picks the tree level that counts as a pass, 0 being the root actions; name_filter narrows the list without a second replay. Triangle counts are derived from the API draw parameters, so they are estimates listed in estimate_fields and repeated in the summary. Use to see where the frame's work clusters and which pass owns a target. Not for how long a pass took - use renderdoc_analysis__get_pass_timing.

tools.name: analyze_state_changes
tools.description: Compare adjacent draws' pipeline state and report what changed between each pair, plus the runs of consecutive draws that share an identical state fingerprint and were therefore batchable. The fingerprint covers primitive topology, graphics and compute pipeline objects, per-stage shaders, output and depth targets, vertex and index buffers, viewport and scissor size, blend and depth enables, and cull mode. A section this capture's replay does not expose is reported as null and as an unavailable section rather than dropped, and the walk is bounded by max_events because each draw costs one state read. Use to find redundant state switches. Not for what a single draw was running with - use renderdoc_analysis__get_draw_call_state.

tools.name: get_pass_timing
tools.description: Report GPU duration per pass by joining this driver's timing counter onto the action tree, with each pass's share of the frame, its timed and untimed action counts, and its slowest actions. pass_depth picks the tree level that counts as a pass, 0 being the root actions. A pass reports its own counter sample when the driver sampled it and the sum of its timed actions otherwise, and the method used is reported per pass so a derived number is never read as a measured one. Requires a timing counter: when this driver exposes none the result says so and lists the counters that are available instead of reporting a frame of zero-duration passes. Use after renderdoc_perf__list_counters when you want to pin counter_id. Not for the pass structure without durations - use renderdoc_analysis__analyze_render_passes.

tools.name: diff_draws
tools.description: Compare one region of one texture or render target between two events of the same capture and report PSNR, mean and max absolute difference, a per-channel breakdown, the share of texels over a threshold, an approximate SSIM, and separate NaN and Inf counts, with an optional difference heatmap export. One replay is reused and moved between the two events, so this is the cheap half of the diff pair. PSNR is reported with its basis - bit depth, channels, and where max_value came from - and two identical regions report identical=true instead of an infinite PSNR. The SSIM here is an approximation over 8x8 blocks with a box window on a sampling grid, reported as ssim_approx with its block size, window, and grid step so it is never mistaken for the standard 11x11 Gaussian SSIM. Requires an uncompressed numeric format; block-compressed, packed, and special formats come back as a structured unsupported result naming the reason. Use for "did this draw change the target?" and as the pixel half of a CI assertion gate. Not for two different captures - use renderdoc_analysis__diff_captures.

tools.name: diff_captures
tools.description: Compare one region of one texture or render target between two captures and report PSNR, mean and max absolute difference, a per-channel breakdown, the share of texels over a threshold, an approximate SSIM, and separate NaN and Inf counts, with an optional difference heatmap export. Each capture is replayed in its own process, because a RenderDoc replay context holds one capture at a time; the texels are handed over through a temporary directory and compared in bounded chunks. The second replay is allowed to fail on its own and is then reported as a one-sided unsupported_capture result, so a capture that will not open is never compared against nothing. match_by picks how the two captures are lined up: event_id for a known id, index for the nth draw, name for the draw with that name. A size, format, or API mismatch returns comparable=false with the reason instead of raising; force compares the region the two sides have in common anyway. PSNR carries its basis - bit depth, channels, and where max_value came from - and two identical regions report identical=true rather than an infinite PSNR. ssim_approx is an approximation over 8x8 blocks with a box window on a sampling grid and is reported with its block size, window, and grid step. Use for regression checks across builds and as the pixel half of a CI assertion gate. Not for two events of one capture - use renderdoc_analysis__diff_draws.

tools.name: assert_pixels
tools.description: Assert that the difference between two draws of one capture, or between two captures, stays inside thresholds you supply, and report the pass/fail verdict with the measured value for every threshold checked. This is the CI gate built on top of diff_draws and diff_captures: it delegates the measurement to them so there is one implementation of the comparison, then turns the numbers into a verdict. At least one of max_mean_abs_diff, min_psnr, or max_failed_pixel_ratio is required, because a gate with no criterion always passes. Two identical regions satisfy any min_psnr, since their PSNR is infinite. When the two sides cannot be compared the result reports evaluable=false rather than passing or failing, so a setup problem never reads as a green build. NaN and Inf texels are excluded from the metrics and reported under non_finite rather than gated on, since they are not one of the thresholds this tool enforces. tools.name: act
tools.description: Perform one scoped semantic or DCC UI Control action. Supports control ids, snapshot coordinates, pointer paths, text, and key presses where the selected backend supports them. Request policy may narrow or deny raw input. Every Windows mutation requires an adapter/operator-bound PID/HWND so the visible capsule and user interruption monitor cover semantic UIA as well as raw input. Raw input is enabled by default inside that exact bound scope and can be disabled with DCC_MCP_CUA_ALLOW_RAW_INPUT=false. Passwords, authentication codes, and other credential material require a user hand-off or a host-owned secure credential flow. The type action is backend-specific to mock/CDP and is not a portable Windows action. Windows keypress rejects ordinary printable, Shift-text, and AltGr-text input; use only navigation/control/function keys or genuine Ctrl/Alt shortcuts. Windows game_navigation is the separately governed game-canvas path: it accepts up to four simultaneous supported canvas keys or `+` chords and an optional 0..500 ms hold, while preserving the existing raw-text denial. For application menu bars, invoke_menu resolves an explicit native menu_path inside the exact bound window. Prefer it when semantic menu clicks or Alt mnemonics cannot prove that a Qt popup opened; it never guesses pixels and always requires a fresh snapshot for verification. For a custom-drawn DCC canvas or face control that has no semantic node, use a path from the latest snapshot for one drag; Ctrl, Shift, and Alt in keys are held as pointer modifiers. They cannot enumerate or target another process/window; restore/show/activate invalidate any prior snapshot and are audited. desktop_unavailable means no Windows UI input was sent; keep the logical session, stop issuing UI calls, and ask the user to unlock or reconnect. tools.name: import_to_scene
tools.description: Import an OBJ asset into ZBrush, adding a subtool when the active tool already contains editable geometry. Suppresses scripted action drawing and UI redraws during import. Accepts an AssetDescriptor-shaped payload (asset_id + variants with local_path/format fields). Returns an ImportToSceneResult with the list of imported subtool names and any non-fatal warnings.

variants.description: One or more file variants; each must have a local_path field.

local_path.description: Absolute or relative path to the asset file on disk.

format.description: File format hint. Only obj supports unattended import.

preferred.description: Whether this variant is preferred for import.

unit_hint.description: Unit hint: meter, centimeter, inch, or unitless.

up_axis.description: Up-axis of the source asset: y or z.

material_mode.description: Material import mode: as_authored, default_gray, or skip.

skills.name: zbrush-interchange
skills.description: Domain skill — export meshes from ZBrush to interchange formats. Use when you need OBJ export from the active subtool. Not for in-scene sculpt edits — use zbrush-subtool first to pick the correct subtool.

tools.name: export_active_subtool_obj
tools.description: Export the currently active subtool to an OBJ file on disk. Overwrites an existing file at output_path. Suppresses scripted action drawing and UI redraws during export. Requires the parent directory to exist.

output_path.description: Absolute or relative path for the exported OBJ file.

skills.name: zbrush-scene
skills.description: Domain skill — read-only scene and tool introspection for ZBrush. Use when you need active tool path, subtool inventory, or selection index. Not for sculpting, export, or subtool mutation — use zbrush-subtool or zbrush-interchange.

tools.name: execute_python
tools.description: Execute a Python snippet inside ZBrush's embedded interpreter. Mutates globals and may change the scene. Prefer typed zbrush-scene / zbrush-subtool / zbrush-interchange tools when available. Returns stdout, stderr, and an optional `result` variable from the namespace.

code.description: Python source executed with `zbc` pre-bound to zbrush.commands.

context.description: Optional extra names injected into the execution namespace.
